$description: Rhythm and adjacency rules JSON Schema cannot express. Every rule below was checked against templates/templates.json's ACTUAL node sequences at the moment it was written (MASTER-GUIDE 3.18) — the exceptions listed are real templates that genuinely violate the blanket rule, not hypotheticals. Each rule id here has a matching implementation in schema/semantic_validate.py; extraction/verify_all.py enforces that the two lists stay in sync.

rules.description: A PageSpec may contain at most one section in the `hero` category.
rules.exceptionReason: form.single has NO hero at all — /contact's entire body is conversion.contact-form. The rule is therefore 'at most one', and zero is legal for this template specifically. Verified against templates.json: form.single's nodes contain no hero.* section.

rules.description: When a hero is present it must be the first node after chrome.navbar.
Every PageSpec must open with chrome.navbar and close with chrome.footer. These are mounted outside the router in the real app, so no route can omit or reposition them.
When conversion.final-cta is present it must be the last node before chrome.footer.
rules.note: Applies conditionally — two templates legitimately omit the section entirely (see FINAL_CTA_OPTIONAL_TEMPLATES).

rules.description: Most templates close on conversion.final-cta. Two do not, by design.
rules.exceptionReason: index.posts closes on conversion.newsletter instead. form.single has no closing section at all — /contact was confirmed live to have no .splash element and to load no nature-desk.jpg. Verified against templates.json: neither template's nodes contain conversion.final-cta.

rules.description: The same section id may not appear in two adjacent positions.
rules.note: home.landing does use content.card-grid twice, but at positions 2 and 6 — never adjacent. This rule keys on (section, variant) so a future page legitimately repeating a section with a different variant is still checked positionally rather than blanket-rejected.

rules.description: content.card-grid may appear at most twice on one page.
rules.evidence: Two is the real observed maximum, on home.landing ('Move at agent speed' and 'Scale with confidence'). Every other template uses it once or not at all. This is a measured ceiling, not an invented one.

rules.description: Sections whose contract declares onePerPage may appear at most once.
hero.scroll-dashboard may only appear on the `/` route.
rules.evidence: The scroll-scrubbed hero is implemented in src/components/Hero.jsx and rendered only by src/pages/Home.jsx. No other page imports it.

rules.description: A PageSpec's nodes must be a valid SUBSEQUENCE of its declared template's node list: every required node present, in order, with no node the template does not declare. This is the cross-reference between the `template` field and `nodes[]` — validating nodes[] in isolation is the single most repeated bug class in this methodology (MASTER-GUIDE 3.3).
Every node's motion object must declare a reducedMotionFallback, and the value must be one the section's own contract allows.
At most 3 nodes per page may use a non-`none` motion pattern.
rules.evidence: home.landing, the most animated page on the site, has 5 non-`none` motion nodes: chrome.navbar (entrance-stagger), hero.scroll-dashboard (scroll-scrub-reveal), interactive.tab-stage and interactive.code-explorer (opacity-crossfade), and social.investor-wall (filter-collapse). The real homepage therefore WARNS against this budget. That is deliberate and verified by running the validator against schema/fixtures/home.landing.pagespec.json: the budget is advisory, and the honest calibration is that the site's busiest page sits above it. Every other template is at or under 2.

rules.description: Every media reference must carry an assetRole drawn from the closed enum in assets/asset-roles.json. A bare image path or an invented role id is rejected.
A node may not reference an assetRole whose aiGuidance is `must-not-fabricate` while also declaring a generated/synthesised asset. Compliance rule — see assets/asset-roles.json globalProhibitions.

Every field in a section contract's own `content.required` list must be present on the node. JSON Schema cannot express this (its per-section branches only const-lock motion), so semantic_validate.py enforces it.
rules.provenance: Added after a second-pass recheck found a control fixture silently missing two required CTA fields on interactive.tab-stage, because nothing cross-referenced each contract's own required list. The gap was in the validator, not just the fixture.

rules.description: A section contract declaring `additionalProperties: false` rejects any content field it does not declare, closing the same hole at the content layer that the schema closes at the node layer.
